description_full: NetApp, Inc. develops enterprise software, systems, and services to transform data infrastructures in the United States, Canada, Latin America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Asia Pacific. It operates through two segments, Hybrid Cloud and Public Cloud. The company offers data management software, such as NetApp ONTAP, ONTAP One, NetApp Snapshot, NetApp SnapCenter Backup Management, NetApp SnapMirror Data Replication, and NetApp SnapLock Data Compliance; and storage infrastructure solutions, including NetApp AFF and ASA A-Series and C-Series, NetApp AFX, NetApp Fabric Attached Storage (FAS), NetApp E/EF series, and NetApp StorageGRID. It also provides cloud storage services comprising Azure NetApp Files, Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP, and Google Cloud NetApp Volumes, as well as NetApp Cloud Volumes ONTAP. In addition, the company offers operational services, such as NetApp Data Infrastructure Insights and Instaclustr; and professional and support services include storage-as-a-service (STaaS), strategic consulting, professional, managed, and support services, as well as assessment, design, implementation, migration, and proactive support services to optimize the performance and efficiency of their on-premises and hybrid multicloud storage environments. Further, it offers ransomware protection, data backup and recovery, and disaster recovery. It serves various industries comprising energy, financial services, government, technology, internet, life sciences, healthcare services, manufacturing, media, entertainment, animation, video postproduction, and telecommunications through a direct sales force and an ecosystem of partners, including the cloud providers. The company has a strategic alliance with Commvault Systems, Inc. to develop an integrated solution for enterprise data protection and cyber resilience; and Super Micro Computer, Inc. to build integrated AI infrastructure solutions. NetApp, Inc. was incorporated in 1992 and is based in San Jose, California.

financial_summary: NetApp, Inc. is a large-cap technology business with a $31.0B market cap on $6.2B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -1% over the past three years and +1% annually across the full decade — essentially flat, and a business treading water is rarely a path to compounding.
Returns on capital run at 284% against a 11% cost of capital — a 274-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 65% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $1.9B in free cash flow — roughly 30 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.62× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 15× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 4.4% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 35% below the high.

val: The stock trades 25% below its DCF fair value of $209, a meaningful margin of safety.

Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 6.0% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 5.2% (vs the 8% bar).
The 16 covering analysts target $212 on average, 34% above the price.
prof: ROIC of 284% clears the cost of capital of 10.6% by 274pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have been steady (CV 0.26).
It runs a 65% gross margin and converts 30% of revenue into free cash flow, or 24% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 8/9 and cash conversion of 1.62x.
ROE of 94% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (8.0x equity multiplier).

hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $1.1B (4% of market cap).

growth: Revenue has compounded at -0.7% over 3 years, 1.7% over 5 years and 1.2% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating.

Free cash flow has compounded 9.8% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.05 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 70% of annual revenue and deferred revenue up 7%.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.1x, 3.2% of sales), a maintenance pace.
Its Rule of 40 score is 26, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.3%), and institutions hold 99%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (12 sales, net $25.8M sold).
It returns 4.4% a year to shareholders (3.1% in buybacks and 1.3% in dividends).

It has paid a dividend for 12 consecutive years, though it has been cut 0.7% a year over the last five.
